args.text: Background: Atrial fibrillation is the most common sustained arrhythmia and is associated with a fivefold increase in the risk of stroke. Methods: We conducted a randomised controlled trial in 1,204 patients aged 65 years or older across 14 centres in Europe between 2015 and 2019. Patients were assigned to apixaban 5 mg twice daily or to warfarin with a target international normalised ratio of 2.0 to 3.0. The primary outcome was stroke or systemic embolism; the primary safety outcome was major bleeding according to ISTH criteria. Results: Over a median follow-up of 2.1 years, stroke or systemic embolism occurred in 1.27% per year in the apixaban group and 1.60% per year in the warfarin group (hazard ratio 0.79; 95% CI 0.66 to 0.95). Major bleeding occurred in 2.13% per year with apixaban versus 3.09% per year with warfarin. Conclusions: In elderly patients with atrial fibrillation, apixaban was superior to warfarin in preventing stroke or systemic embolism, caused less bleeding and resulted in lower mortality.
